lines.en: At first, I thought I had misheard.
But as the demon kings' gazes poured down on me, Asmodeus applauded me, and I took in my companions' bewildered faces—it slowly began to sink in.
<Kim Dokja’s Company> had won the Grand Prize.
Yet unease outweighed my joy.
The Grand Prize? Us?
Here, of all places, at the ‘Duet between Good and Evil’?
The source of my unease soon became clear.
[This year's winning work has not yet been classified as good or evil.]
At the message that it had yet to be classified as good or evil, several demon kings and constellations stirred at once.
[Not classified as good or evil? What does that mean?]
The dokkaebi answered immediately.

[Historically, Grand Prize winners have been chosen by agreement between the great dokkaebis and the constellations of Absolute Good and Absolute Evil. But this time, for the first time, no conclusion was reached.]
[······No conclusion? Those ‘great dokkaebis’ couldn't reach one?]
The constellations and demon kings all looked taken aback.
Of course the constellations belonging to Absolute Good or Absolute Evil would favor their own side, but even the great dokkaebis had failed to agree.
[Nothing like this has happened since the ‘Duet between Good and Evil’ was established. No, not since the Great War of Saints and Demons (聖魔大戰) ended!]
[Impossible to classify? No such story can exist. The scales of good and evil must tip one way or the other!]
The agitated constellations and demon kings traded shouts.
It wasn't that I couldn't understand them.
In most Giant Story scenarios, agreements or manipulation by the nebulas determined the winner.

Just as <Gigantomachia> had been sold as a kind of tourist attraction, the winner in other Giant Story scenarios—good or evil—was already decided, as though preferred shares (優先株) were being sold off.
But our Story, born from bringing down <Gigantomachia>, had come into being in an entirely different way.
A Story born from the collapse of a Giant Story scenario run by none other than <Olympus>.
Since it had never been planned in the first place, it couldn't have been classified as good or evil in advance.
The dokkaebi smiled as though finding this amusing.

[Well, how could someone like me know what the great dokkaebis think? In any case, this Grand Prize winner will be judged good or evil right here. Anyone with an opinion, please raise your hand and speak.]
Only then did the dokkaebi's intention become clear.
······These damned bastards.
Whether <Kim Dokja’s Company> won an award had never mattered to them. What mattered was whether the Story we had built was good or evil—and how that would change their own standing.
[Of course that Story is ‘evil’.]
The first to speak was the 50th-ranked demon king, ‘Duke of Everywhere’.
Duke of Everywhere. His true name was Furcas, master of the 50th Demon Realm.
[The ‘Demon King of Salvation’ is a ‘demon king’. A dim-witted one, admittedly, but he is still master of a Demon Realm. Therefore, all his actions must be evil.]
Pathetic logic, just as expected from the Duke of Everywhere, who couldn't even spell properly.
Then someone on the opposing side raised a hand.
[Yeah, I object to that.]
It was Raphael, ‘Guardian of Youths and Travel’. Raphael clicked his tongue—tsk, tsk—and wagged a finger before he began.

[Say someone stole something and became an evildoer. The whole world called him evil, so that's what he became. But it turns out he used the stolen money to save people. What if he saved loads of people, giving bread to the poor and water to the thirsty?]
I nodded at Raphael's argument.
[Is he still an ‘evildoer’, then? Just because he was labeled one once?]
[Well, that is······ I mean.]
The Duke of Everywhere, no great speaker, was caught in Raphael's logic.
Then the demon king beside me raised a hand to help him.
[Are you proposing we discuss the ‘paradox of the good evildoer’ here?]
Asmodeus's red eyes were alight with excitement.
Come to think of it, Asmodeus owed Raphael one.
Raphael nodded.
[Sure. If you want.]
Lying on his stomach on a cloud bed, Raphael snapped his fingers.
Scenes of my companions and me taking part in <Gigantomachia> began playing on the stage's giant screen.
Watching the screen, Raphael continued.
[In the end, a being is made of Stories, and a Story is made of the sum of that being's actions. But however you look at it, it's hard to find any evil in the events piled up in this Story.]
「The Paradox of the Good Evildoer」.
This paradox implied that whether a being was ‘good or evil’ was defined by the stories that being had accumulated.
Raphael pointed at the split screens and spoke.
The first showed me visiting the Underworld and freeing the giants.
[The ‘Demon King of Salvation’ freed the weak who were being unjustly oppressed in the scenarios.]
The second showed my companions resisting <Gigantomachia>, now a tourist attraction, alongside the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint.
[The members of <Kim Dokja’s Company> opposed the unjust structure of the <Gigantomachia> scenario.]
The last, as expected, showed my companions and me burning the sacred flame as we faced Poseidon, a Myth-grade constellation.
[They fought an irresistible force to overthrow a great nebula's ruling system. Look. Where exactly can you find ‘evil’ in what's happened so far?]
Many constellations nodded as Raphael explained his points through the details of each scene.
The demon kings, on the other hand, were grimacing.
All except Asmodeus, to be precise.
[How interesting. With such protection from the angels, perhaps the ‘Demon King of Salvation’ really is a ‘good demon king’.]
[So you admit it?]
[No. There is a flaw in your argument. Let us first accept, as you say, that ‘a being is a Story’, and a Story is ‘the sum of events’.]
Asmodeus smiled and glanced at me.
[As you know, a Story never exists alone. One Story is necessarily connected to others and affects them. 「Torch That Eats the Myth」 is no exception.]
At that moment, a different scene began playing on the screen ahead.
It was a scene from the first scenario, long ago.
The screen showed a close-up of a gravid grasshopper's eggs, burst open by my hand.
[The ‘Demon King of Salvation’ let people die on the subway. Even though he could have saved every one of them.]
Some angels looked at me dubiously.
Asmodeus continued.
[There was also this occasion.]
The next image was the ‘eighth scenario’.
The scenario in which everyone could live if Seoul's strongest incarnation sacrificed themselves.
The screen showed me with ‘eight lives’ granted by my attribute.
Asmodeus said,
[The ‘Demon King of Salvation’ had spare lives and knew he was ‘The Strongest Sacrifice’. Had he wished, he could have ended the scenario before any greater sacrifices were made.]
The constellations' murmurs grew louder. The account continued.

[Someone who saves those he wishes to save, and stands by while unwanted lives perish. That is the ‘Demon King of Salvation’. A demon king who practices the discrimination you so despise. ‘Discrimination’, the most terrible sin in this <Star Stream>.]
As though declaring victory, Asmodeus posed his final question.
[I ask you, <Eden>. Do you still consider the ‘Demon King of Salvation’ a ‘good demon king’?]
The room fell silent.
Some angels watched me suspiciously, while many demon kings were smiling broadly.
Then one constellation sprang to their feet.
[■■, everyone has contradictions like that.]
It was Uriel.
[What matters isn't the sins piling up, but the direction in which those events change someone. And the ‘Demon King of Salvation’ was heading in a just direction!]
[Angels are remarkably lenient about defining good and evil these days. I've heard rumors that you have recently developed a personal fondness for a demon king. Is that true?]
[What?]
[Hmm, it seems it is. I wondered when I saw you last time, but—]
Uriel shot to her feet.
[You ■ of a ■■, how dare you······!]
Bzzzzzt······!
Enormous sparks began flying around the two tables. Archangels and demon kings hurled abuse, and soon opinions erupted from every direction.
Now I wasn't even the only target.
Someone attacked Jung Heewon's killings.
Someone else attacked Lee Hyunsung's cowardice in the first scenario.
Someone else kept harping on how Lee Jihye had killed her friend.
Our lives (生), the histories we had built, were being hacked to pieces.
[The Story, ‘Torch That Swallowed the Myth’, bares its teeth.]
My companions were gradually turning pale.
People who had already suffered wounds they could barely bear.
People who had somehow held on this far, putting up with their lives being voyeuristically watched and made into entertainment for the constellations.
[Wait! You don't have to go this far, do you?]
Uriel shouted, realizing something too late, but the constellations and demon kings were already busy digging into <Kim Dokja’s Company>'s wounds.
In the end, they even began picking apart Shin Yoosung's and Lee Gilyoung's pasts.
I stepped forward at last when Lee Gilyoung's trauma and sponsor were mentioned.
“That is enough.”
At my words, everyone instantly turned toward me.
I knew saying the wrong thing here would be dangerous.
Right now, <Kim Dokja’s Company> was like a sailboat caught between two enormous currents. A small boat that could sink at any time if it rode the wrong current.
But no matter how small a boat was, it could at least choose where it would go.
And I was its captain.
“Haven't you done enough? Surely you've realized by now that you won't reach a conclusion?”
I hadn't intervened until now because I had been waiting for the constellations and demon kings to contradict themselves.
“Do you think you can decide something here that even the great dokkaebis couldn't judge?”
<Kim Dokja’s Company> was neither good nor evil.
I had never had the slightest intention of being toyed with by someone else's definitions of ‘good and evil’.
[He is right.]
Unexpectedly, the speaker was ‘Black Mane Lion’, Marbas, the fifth-ranked demon king. He looked at me and continued.
[Indeed, our chatter here serves no purpose. Let us end this unnecessary debate.]
[Marbas! But······.]
[We need only ask the person in question.]
I felt my spine creak.
[Let him decide for himself. Whether this ‘Story’ is good or evil. Isn't that why this gathering was arranged?]
At those words, every demon king and constellation turned their gaze on me.
Cold sweat ran down my spine, sending a chill through me.
Then system messages appeared.
[You hold a stake in the Giant Story, ‘Torch That Swallowed the Myth’.]
[Please determine whether this Story is good or evil.]
If I chose good or evil here, I would be taking one of the sides they called ‘good’ and ‘evil’. That would be a problem.
It wasn't just <Kim Dokja’s Company>'s course at stake. Choosing good or evil here could mean a terrible future in the scenarios to come.
After thinking for a long time, I finally decided.
Even if the constellations or demon kings condemned me, it couldn't be helped.
“The Giant Story, ‘Torch That Swallowed the Myth’, is—”
“Good (善).”
I stared blankly at the protagonist who had spoken.
The man in the black coat, who had remained silent until now.
Yoo Joonghyuk was speaking.
“This Story is good.”
I was so flustered that all I could do was open and close my mouth.
I wondered whether Yoo Joonghyuk had gone mad, or whether he had fallen into some trap.
Metatron, seated beside him, was smiling faintly at me.
Goosebumps slowly rose on my arms.
Could the reason Metatron had brought Yoo Joonghyuk be······.
[Beings with stakes in this ‘Giant Story’ may assert the right to judge whether it is ‘good or evil’.]
At the next message, the constellations' and demon kings' mouths opened slightly.
[Incarnation ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’ holds a 22.8% stake in the Giant Story, ‘Torch That Swallowed the Myth’.
[The declaration of incarnation ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’ has tipped the Story toward ‘good’.]
I wasn't the only one who could define this Story as ‘good’ or ‘evil’.
Because everyone in <Kim Dokja’s Company> held a stake in it.
[Will you approve this Story as ‘good’?]
Yoo Joonghyuk was watching me.
His expression unreadable. As though asking what I would do now.
—You lunatic! What the hell are you thinking!
I spoke to him through [Midday Tryst], but Yoo Joonghyuk didn't answer.
I glared at him, then activated a skill.
[Activating the exclusive skill, ‘Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint’!]
[This person is currently experiencing emotions you cannot understand.]
[If no other storyteller objects, this Story will be confirmed as ‘good’.]
[30 seconds remain until confirmation.]
I couldn't understand what was happening.
As the numbers dwindled, I heard the demon kings shouting.
I looked at my startled companions.
Jung Heewon, Lee Hyunsung, Shin Yoosung, Lee Gilyoung······.
The people I wanted to bring with me to the end of this world, no matter what.
I clenched my fists with a crunch.
Our Story must never be defined as good or evil by the constellations' standards.
If that happened, I couldn't reach this world's proper ending.
Now that Yoo Joonghyuk had declared ‘good’, there was only one way to overturn the verdict.
[The demon king, ‘Demon King of Salvation’, reveals his Status.]
Black-feathered wings breaking through my shoulder blades, and small horns sprouting on my head.
With a fierce burst of sparks, all the murmuring subsided at once.
Drawing a slow breath, I glared at Yoo Joonghyuk and spoke.
[This Story is evil (惡).]
At my declaration, system messages flickered in the air.
[You are currently this Story's Supreme Storyteller.]
[You hold a 33.7% stake in the Giant Story, 'Torch That Swallowed the Myth'.]
[Your declaration has tipped the Story toward 'evil'.]
My alarmed companions rose from their seats.
I raised a hand to reassure them, then sent Yoo Joonghyuk a [Midday Tryst] message.
-Yoo Joonghyuk, at this rate our Story will be confirmed as 'evil'. That isn't what you want, is it?
My stake in [Torch That Swallowed the Myth] was 33.7%
And Yoo Joonghyuk's was 22.8%
I was ahead by a full 10.9%.
[The two storytellers currently hold opposing opinions.]
[Storytellers, please reach an agreement on whether the Story is good or evil.]
[If no agreement is reached within the time limit, the verdict will follow the choice of the larger stakeholder.]
[The judgment period has been extended by 10 minutes.]
Yoo Joonghyuk didn't answer.
I sent another message.
-I don't know what you're thinking, but 'good or evil' can't be decided here. Withdraw your declaration now. Then I'll withdraw mine too.
[The constellation, 'Guardian of Youths and Travel', glares at you]
[The demon king, 'Devil of Lust and Wrath', is delighted by your judgment.]
[The constellation, 'Demon-like Judge of Fire', is bewildered by your judgment.]
I was sorry to do this to Uriel, but we absolutely couldn't let the Story be classified as good or evil here.
[The demon king, 'Ruler of Eastern Hell', takes a liking to you.]
The seat of honor among the demon kings.
The master of the second Demon Realm, 'Ruler of Eastern Hell', was looking at me with satisfaction.
There seemed to be a misunderstanding. I hadn't stepped forward to side with 'evil'.
Growing anxious, I shouted again.
-Hey! Can't you hear me?
Then Yoo Joonghyuk moved.
Stepping past the table onto the stage, he drew his sword with a shing.
[Incarnation 'Yoo Joonghyuk' refuses to reach an agreement with you.]
I dodged his blade almost reflexively.
The table split, and the stage became a shambles in an instant.
As the startled demon kings shouted, I too drew a sword from inside my coat and gripped it.
Yoo Joonghyuk's [Black Heavenly Demon Sword] and my [Unbreakable Faith] collided with a sharp crack. My throbbing wrist.
"You crazy...."
Uriel tried to rush over in alarm, but a blue barrier on the stage blocked the constellations' movements.
Bzzzzzt!
[Constellations and demon kings participating in the 'Duet between Good and Evil' cannot act against one another!]
[Assistance from other constellations in a stake-based judgment is prohibited.]
This was the worst possible situation.
[The great dokkaebi, 'Baram', anticipates your choice.]
[The great dokkaebi, 'Halong', watches as you decide.]
Even the great dokkaebis had revealed their presence.
The Bureau, too, was watching the judgment of our Story's 'good or evil'.
This scenario was probably being relayed through another Star Stream broadcasting channel right now.
Rooooar!
I glared at Yoo Joonghyuk, whose Status was growing stronger.
An unreadable face.
I didn't know why he had suddenly started this.
But I couldn't yield to this ignorant third-round bastard.
-Yoo Joonghyuk, you won't understand right now, but listen carefully.
Somehow, I had to convince him.
-If our Story is fixed as good or evil here, a terrible disaster will happen.
According to the original novel, this season would mark a turning point in Absolute Good and Absolute Evil's battle of pride.
Over the past several seasons of the 'Duet between Good and Evil', 'good' had consistently won the Grand Prize.
In other words, the demon kings were sharpening their knives for this 'Duet between Good and Evil'.
If good won here, the 'Second Great War of Saints and Demons' would break out.
If evil won instead, <Eden> would lose ground, hastening its destruction.
The Stories I had accumulated weren't yet at the level needed to face the Great War of Saints and Demons.
But I didn't want to let 'evil' win, either.
-I'll explain the details later. For now, just listen....
"Is that your 'prophecy'?"
A deep shadow of distrust flickered in Yoo Joonghyuk's burning eyes.
Prophecy.
Come to think of it, I had introduced myself as a 'Prophet' when we first met.
I hadn't known he still believed that. Under the circumstances, I thought that might be for the best. But before I could speak, he asked again.
"Or is it information from that book, 'Ways of Survival'?"
"What?"
My heart suddenly pounded.
How did Yoo Joonghyuk know about 'Ways of Survival'?
[The sponsor of incarnation 'Yoo Joonghyuk' disapproves of this situation.]
[The constellation, 'Demon-like Judge of Fire', does not want you to fight!]
[The constellation, 'Prisoner of the Golden Headband', is confused by this unexpected situation.]
[The constellation, 'Secretive Plotter', watches as you decide.]
Sparks flew all over Yoo Joonghyuk's body.
He frowned deeply, as though suffering a headache.
As if defying some will, he continued.
"If I do as you say, will this scenario end safely too?"
"Yoo Joonghyuk, what are you...."
"Because that is the method I used in a later regression round?"
Rumble!
"Because that is 'how to survive in this world'?"
My grip suddenly went slack.
[The 'Fourth Wall' shakes.]
My surroundings shook, and a small tremor stirred deep inside me. The shaking spread rapidly from its epicenter.
I grabbed my violently trembling right hand.
When I looked up, Yoo Joonghyuk was watching my companions over my shoulder.
-Do they know?
Just how much did Yoo Joonghyuk know?
-Answer me, Kim Dokja.
The echo of Status flowing from [Black Heavenly Demon Sword] intensified.
Yoo Joonghyuk unleashing his power as a transcendent.
He truly had no intention of going easy on me now.
[The character, 'Yoo Joonghyuk', sets a 'Giant Story' in motion.]
[The Giant Story, 'Torch That Swallowed the Myth', begins its story!]
I couldn't let him have his way.
[You are this Story's Supreme Storyteller.]
[Your restraining power controls the Story.]
[The Giant Story, 'Torch That Swallowed the Myth', is dissatisfied with your 'Status'.]
[The Giant Story, 'Torch That Swallowed the Myth', refuses your rule.]
....What?
Despite my large stake, the Story wouldn't listen to me.
Our sacred flame, which had shattered Poseidon's barrier, was winding around Yoo Joonghyuk's [Black Heavenly Demon Sword].
Those pure white flames were approaching, step by step, to swallow me.
[The exclusive skill, 'Fourth Wall', activates strongly!]
[(Dokja-ssi, snap out of it!)]
At Yoo Sangah's words, I released my Status.
[The Giant Story, 'Demon Realm's Spring', protects you.]
[The Giant Story, 'Torch That Swallowed the Myth', shows hostility toward you!]
The two Stories we had built together tangled and collided in midair.
Torch That Swallowed the Myth bit and tore at Demon Realm's Spring like a ferocious beast. Torn strings of text scattered through the air like blood.
"What are you two doing! Are you out of your minds?"
[Incarnation 'Jung Heewon' intervenes in the judgment of the 'Giant Story'!]
"Master! What's gotten into you? And why did you choose 'evil', ajusshi!"
[Incarnation 'Lee Jihye' intervenes in the judgment of the 'Giant Story'!]
"Dokja-ssi! Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi! Both of you, stop!"
[Incarnation 'Lee Hyunsung' intervenes in the judgment of the 'Giant Story'!]
"Stop picking on my hyung, you black-coated jerk!"
[Incarnation 'Lee Gilyoung' intervenes in the judgment of the 'Giant Story'!]
"Ajusshi! Dodge!"
[Incarnation 'Shin Yoosung' intervenes in the judgment of the 'Giant Story'!]
Their help was welcome right now.
Torch That Swallowed the Myth—a Story that belonged to us all.
In other words, Yoo Joonghyuk and I weren't the only ones who could judge it.
[Storytellers who have intervened in the judgment, please determine whether the Story is good or evil.]
[You cannot join the confrontation without choosing good or evil.]
My companions looked confused.
Being told to choose good or evil out of nowhere would bewilder anyone.
Amid the confusion, Lee Gilyoung spoke first.
"I'm on Dokja-hyung's side, no matter what."
[Incarnation 'Lee Gilyoung' holds a 3.3% stake in the Giant Story, 'Torch That Swallowed the Myth'.]
[The declaration of incarnation 'Lee Gilyoung' has tipped the Story toward 'evil'.]
I shouted quickly.
"No one else choose 'evil'! Everyone, choose 'good!"
"What?"
"Do as I say! Quickly!"
If I couldn't make Yoo Joonghyuk withdraw his declaration, there was only one way left.
Bring these damned scales of good and evil into perfect balance.
The current difference was 14.2%.
If I added up the other four people's stakes....
"Choose slowly, one at a time! Yoosung first!"
"Okay"
[Incarnation 'Shin Yoosung' holds a 3.3% stake in the Giant Story, 'Torch That Swallowed the Myth'.]
[Incarnation 'Jung Heewon' holds a 6.7% stake in the Giant Story, 'Torch That Swallowed the Myth'.]
[Incarnation 'Lee Hyunsung' holds a 7.3% stake in the Giant Story, 'Torch That Swallowed the Myth'.]
[Three storytellers have chosen 'good'.]
"Stop!"
Lee Jihye, about to make the final choice, halted at my shout.
[The scales now favor 'good' by 3.1%!]
[If no agreement is reached within the next 5 minutes, 'Torch That Swallowed the Myth' will be confirmed as 'good'.]
My companions held larger stakes in the Story than I'd expected.
Now only Lee Jihye remained.
"Ajusshi! I have 5.8%!"
The difference between good and evil was 3.1%
And Lee Jihye held a 5.8% stake.
Whichever side she chose, she couldn't balance the scales.
My thoughts raced.
....What if I could bring just a portion of the others' 'stakes' over to my side?
['Stake transfers' between storytellers participating in the good-and-evil judgment are prohibited.]
Damn it. Of course an easy way out like that wouldn't work.
Yoo Joonghyuk's [Black Heavenly Demon Sword] flew toward my neck again.
"I said stop!"

Now able to join the duel, Jung Heewon blocked Yoo Joonghyuk's sword for me. Lee Hyunsung rushed in and wrapped his arms around him from behind, while the children surrounded me protectively. Lee Jihye stood between us, not knowing what to do.
"Why the hell are you two fighting! Of all times, now....!"
Yoo Joonghyuk's eyes moved between my companions and me.
He seemed to want to say something.
No, in fact, I thought I knew what he wanted to say.
You're being deceived
His trembling eyes poured their anger toward me.
That bastard has deceived us all
I had thought this day would come.
In truth, I thought about it dozens of times a day.
"Get lost, all of you"
Amplifying his Status, Yoo Joonghyuk sent Lee Hyunsung flying, knocked Lee Jihye down, then charged toward me. Jung Heewon's sword clashed with his.
But unable to activate [Hour of Judgement], Jung Heewon couldn't possibly be a match for Yoo Joonghyuk.
I moved the children back and stepped forward.
[The demon king, 'Monarch of Stars and Logic', cheers you on.]
[The demon king, 'Demon God of Necromancy', wants you to win.]
[The constellation, 'Morning Star Goddess', wants good to triumph.]
[Many constellations and demon kings watch <Kim Dokja’s Company>.]
Messages from the constellations voyeuristically watching me as I stepped forward.
Why were they so obsessed with 'good' and 'evil'?
[The exclusive skill, 'Reading Comprehension', activates!]
.....Perhaps I already knew the answer.
They had no choice.
[The Story, 'Practitioner of Encouraging Good and Punishing Evil', continues its story.]
[The Story, 'Guardian of a Hundred Evils (百惡)', continues its story.]
[The Story, 'More Evil than Evil', continues its story.]
[The Story, 'The Suitable Good', continues its story.]
Countless strings of text swarmed like insects in the eyes of the constellations and demon kings.
The Stories they possessed. Stories that controlled them.
They were no longer 'constellations' or 'demon kings'.
Beings who existed only to enact 'good' and 'evil' in this world.
Most were nothing but breeding tools that ancient 'Stories' used to propagate themselves.
At last, those Stories were trying to devour even our nebula's Story.
[If no agreement is reached within the next 2 minutes, 'Torch That Swallowed the Myth' will be confirmed as 'good'.]
I couldn't let that happen.
Quickly making up my mind, I shouted.
"Jihye! Choose 'good'!"
"Huh? But....."
"Hurry!"
Lee Jihye looked as though she didn't understand.
'Good' already had the advantage, so being told to choose it would seem strange. She made her choice at once.
[The scales now favor 'good' by 8.9%!]
[If no agreement is reached within the next 40 seconds, 'Torch That Swallowed the Myth' will be confirmed as 'good'.]
A gap even wider than before.
8.9%..... Yes, this was the best option after all.
Drawing a sharp breath, I called out a certain being's modifier with all my strength.
[Abyssal Black Flame Dragon!]
I knew he was watching.
That meant his incarnation knew what was happening here, too.
The only person who would understand exactly what I wanted in this situation.
[The constellation, 'Abyssal Black Flame Dragon', gives a mad grin.]
Wrapped in a transcendent's Status, Yoo Joonghyuk's [Black Heavenly Demon Sword] shot toward my neck. A blow I couldn't possibly evade.
Then cracks tore across the hall's ceiling, and a deafening crash erupted. Startled, Yoo Joonghyuk looked up, but it was already too late.
Kraaaash!
The charging Yoo Joonghyuk was buried beneath the collapsing ceiling.

He dodged a few large chunks, but there was too much falling stone. A small silhouette appeared through the rising dust. Sweat-soaked hair, as if from a frantic rush to get here. The half-unwound bandage on their left hand fluttered in the wind.
Standing atop Yoo Joonghyuk amid the dust, the figure smiled with a frown.
"Seriously, you people can't do anything without me."
[Incarnation 'Han Sooyoung' intervenes in the judgment of the 'Giant Story'!]
Yoo Joonghyuk's hand stuck out from beneath the rubble.
Han Sooyoung looked down at him and sneered.
“You jerk, you always make your entrance by trampling other people······ Doesn't feel so great when you're the one underneath, does it?”
[Incarnation ‘Han Sooyoung’ holds an 8.9% stake in the Giant Story, ‘Torch That Swallowed the Myth’.]
As expected, I knew Han Sooyoung would bring exactly the right ‘stake’.
The system had said, ‘Stake transfers between storytellers participating in the judgment are prohibited.’ That meant transfers between storytellers who hadn't yet joined were possible.
Giving me a sidelong glare, Han Sooyoung grumbled through [Midday Tryst].
—Thanks to you, Lee Seolhwa took 0.1% off me.
As soon as she learned what was happening here, she had probably adjusted their stakes with Lee Seolhwa. Then she would have come straight here.
Turning toward the surrounding constellations, Han Sooyoung declared with a growl.
“I'm ‘evil’. And that damned Kim Dokja standing there in a daze is definitely ‘evil’, too.”
Having made me evil regardless of my wishes, she looked at Yoo Joonghyuk beneath the rubble, then at our other companions, and continued.
“But <Kim Dokja’s Company> is neither good nor evil.”
She looked so magnificent shouting with her short, bobbed hair flying that, for that moment, Han Sooyoung seemed like the protagonist instead of Yoo Joonghyuk.
[The time limit has expired, ending the judgment of whether this Story is good or evil.]
[The total stake participating in the good-and-evil judgment is 91.8%.]
[The participating proportions of good and evil are 45.9% : 45.9%.]
[The scales of good and evil have reached perfect balance.]
Astonished constellations and demon kings were staring at us.
I turned to them and added,
“We won't be defined by your definitions of ‘justice’.”
[The Giant Story, ‘Torch That Swallowed the Myth’, cannot be classified as good or evil.]

A wounded sword demon was raging.
Having read the original novel, I could predict what she would say next.
「“What the hell were we to you?”」
With her head bowed, Lee Jihye's shoulders trembled slightly.
The coming scene unfolded smoothly in my mind.
She would draw her sword, and might attack me, unable to contain her anger.
That had happened several times in the original novel, too.
But Lee Jihye chose a path I knew nothing about.
“Let's say you knew the future, ajusshi.”
“Let's say all of it was planned, and you used us for your own goals, ajusshi. Let's say we're characters in that damned ‘Ways of Survival’ novel, and everything was predetermined!”
Lee Jihye watched me, crying and biting her bloodless lips.
“Then······ why did you throw your life away for us over and over, ajusshi?”
Watching the tears fall down her cheeks, I tried again and again to speak.
A question I hadn't expected.
A question I couldn't answer because I hadn't foreseen it······.
“Answer me, ajusshi! If we're really ‘characters’ in a novel, why have you died for us again and again all this time!”
A question with no answer in the ‘Ways of Survival’ I had read.
[The ‘Fourth Wall’ shakes violently.]
Wiping her eyes as though frustrated, Lee Jihye brushed past, striking my shoulder.
Jung Heewon hurriedly stood and followed her, saying,
“······Dokja-ssi, let's talk a little later.”

With a helpless expression, Shin Yoosung hesitantly reached toward me, then followed Jung Heewon out. Lee Hyunsung, his eyes blank as though something inside had come loose, also bowed his head and left the room.
Now only Han Sooyoung, Lee Seolhwa, and Lee Gilyoung remained.
Lee Gilyoung watched me with mixed emotions in his eyes, and Lee Seolhwa had lowered her head, perhaps in shock.
Patting Lee Seolhwa's back, Han Sooyoung snapped at me.
“Kim Dokja, go outside for a bit.”
A quiet hospital room. I gazed at my sleeping mother's face. My companions hadn't returned for a long time, so I had used the interval to visit her room.

Ever since her major operation a little while ago, Mother had slept all day like this. Gaunt cheeks and shadows around her eyes. Looking at her pale face reminded me of visiting her in the detention center, long ago.
What had Mother thought, watching her son visit and talk about novels all day?
“You look troubled.”
“······You're awake?”
“Since you came in.”
Her voice hadn't yet regained its strength.
I pulled the rumpled blanket up to cover her neck.
Mother smiled faintly.
“The apocalypse has its merits. I even get to be looked after by my son.”
“Just get better soon.”
“Tell me. Anything will do.”
After hesitating for a moment, I spoke.
“······In the 154th round of ‘Ways of Survival’, when Yoo Joonghyuk told his companions about regression······.”
“You've told your companions about ‘Ways of Survival’, I see.”
“······How did you know?”
Watching me, Mother reached out her thin hand and took mine.
“I thought they'd curse at me. I thought they'd demand to know why I deceived them and hid the information.”
“But it seems they didn't.”
“······I don't know how to ask their forgiveness.”
I nodded silently.
—Answer me, ajusshi! If we're really ‘characters’ in a novel······ why have you died for us again and again all this time!
Lee Jihye's voice lingering in my ears.
Mother said,
“You don't get to decide whether this is a matter of ‘forgiveness’.”
“Perhaps the person behind you can tell you.”
Wondering what she meant, I turned to find Jung Heewon standing at the hospital room's door.
I excused myself to Mother and left the room.
Scratching her cheek, Jung Heewon asked,
“Shall we walk for a bit?”

We walked down the ward's corridor. A simple corridor without a single decoration. It looked like Yoo Joonghyuk's taste······ He seemed to have remodeled the [Factory] however he liked over the past three years. In fact, Yoo Joonghyuk's hospital room was at the end of this ward's corridor.
After looking out the window for a moment, Jung Heewon spoke first.
“Thank you······ for telling us.”
I couldn't know how much she had thought it over before saying that. All the more so because I couldn't see her expression.
Through the window, I saw our companions. Shin Yoosung was bickering with Lee Gilyoung, and Lee Hyunsung and Lee Seolhwa were comforting Lee Jihye.
“Everyone will be all right. Jihye might need a little more time, but······.”
“Heewon-ssi, are you······.”
Before I finished, Jung Heewon turned to look at me. Smiling as she always did. When I closed my mouth, she asked,
“Surprised I'm taking it so well?”
“No.”
“Oh, you are.”
Jung Heewon had known for a long time that I possessed ‘information about the future’. Perhaps she knew more about me than any of the other ‘characters’.
Stretching, Jung Heewon said,
“It's no big deal. We live in a world with monsters and dokkaebis······ What's so special about a novel becoming reality?”
“Anyway, Dokja-ssi, now I understand. When you said I wasn't in the ‘original future’. You meant I wasn't in that novel you mentioned, didn't you?”
Floating like a cloud, Biyoo bounced above Shin Yoosung's head like a chewy rice cake.
Jung Heewon said,
“Then I made it this far thanks to you, Dokja-ssi.”
“Listen, Heewon-ssi—”
“Thank you for finding me. I'm not being sarcastic. I mean it.”
I knew. I was already familiar with the tone she used when teasing me.
But that was precisely why I didn't know what to say.
“Don't go getting gloomy and losing heart all by yourself again. Let's keep working together. And while you're at it, hurry up with my promotion. Here, a handshake to cheer us on.”
Pulling my hand toward her, Jung Heewon gripped it firmly.
At that sudden warmth, something welled up inside me.
I bit my lip hard.
「There was no way Jung Heewon could simply be all right, either.」
I could hear a heartbeat from Jung Heewon's tightly clasped hand.
She would be sad, too. She would be suffering, too. It would be hard for her, too. And yet······.
After holding my hand tightly for a moment, Jung Heewon smiled awkwardly and let go. Then she asked,
“Dokja-ssi, there's······ something I'm curious about.”
“Yes, go ahead.”
“If this world is a ‘novel’, that means there's a protagonist somewhere, doesn't it?”
······As expected, Jung Heewon was perceptive.
I had told my companions about ‘Ways of Survival’, but I hadn't revealed who its protagonist was.
Yet she seemed to have already guessed who that ‘protagonist’ was.
Her gaze drifted toward the end of the ward.
“Is that why you fought?”
“We haven't had a proper conversation about it yet······ but I think so.”
“Since you've started, you have to see it through properly. You know that, right?”
I nodded.
“He won't be easy.”
I knew.
But it wasn't something I could avoid, either.
For the next two days, I spent all day in Yoo Joonghyuk's hospital room.
I hardly saw my other companions. I was worried, but decided to stay calm.
I believed they needed time to think, too. When they were ready, it wouldn't be too late to talk again.
Yoo Joonghyuk still hadn't woken.
“His physical wounds have almost healed, but it seems to be a psychological problem.”
“A psychological problem?”
“It's as though he's refusing to wake up······ Perhaps something happened that gave him a severe shock.”
That was all Aileen said.
After she changed his Story pack and left, only Yoo Joonghyuk and I remained in the room.
A floating speck of dust settled on his nose. Watching him, I spoke without thinking.
“You were the one who grabbed me by the collar and threw me off a bridge first.”
Though I knew he couldn't hear, I wanted to say something.
「“Just let go and fuck off, you goddamn bastard.”
“I'll trust you. You really are a prophet.”」
That day we first met on the bridge. A laugh suddenly escaped me.
“Honestly, you're in no position to criticize me. You're a regressor yourself······ Do you know how many times I nearly died because of you?”
Once I began speaking, memories poured out like a waterfall. Memories spilling out as though I'd touched Pandora's box. I felt anew how much time had passed.
Before I knew it, I had made my way through so much time with him.
“I thought I understood you better than anyone, but these days, I'm not sure. Why did you do that during the ‘Disaster of Floods’?”
「“······He is my companion.”」
“Why did you call me your ‘companion’? You never say things like that······ Then you stabbed me to death in the Dark Castle. ······Though I did tell you to kill me then.”
「“Kim Dokja! No! Kim Dokja!”」
With each memory I retraced, countless emotions rose and faded.
Scenarios that had been so grave at the time became stories once they were past.
They remained as Stories we had built.

“Still, thanks for what you did during the ‘Revolutionary Game’. You saved me then. But that was strange, too. Why did you use my name to attack some unrelated industrial complex? Well······ obviously you were trying to screw me over, but······.”
As I thought about one thing after another, I slowly grew sleepy.
I hadn't been sleeping properly either······.
Even as my consciousness grew hazy, my complaints continued.
The times we had fought together flashed past as though I were reading ‘Ways of Survival’.
Disaster of Questions.
The Strongest Sacrifice.
Peace Land.
The Graveyard of Scenarios.
The Demon King Selection and Gigantomachia······.
It was harder to find a battlefield where I hadn't fought beside him.
Looking back on those times, I thought,
‘Maybe it'll be all right.’
If he was the Yoo Joonghyuk I knew.
Couldn't I convince him somehow?
We had never had a proper conversation, not once.
What if I took the time and explained, little by little?
If it was him, of all people······.
Far away, I dimly saw Yoo Joonghyuk with his back turned.
Forgetting even that this was a dream, I approached him.
‘Yoo Joonghyuk.’
At that moment, words flashed through my mind with a sharp pain.
It was a scene from ‘Ways of Survival’. Yoo Joonghyuk, who had lived in misery for so long after Anna Croft betrayed him.
The last words that Yoo Joonghyuk had left behind.
「“I will never forgive you.”」
Yoo Joonghyuk had turned around and was speaking to me.
Killing intent pouring from the [Black Heavenly Demon Sword] in his hand.
「“Kim Dokja.”」
The moment I felt a chill at the back of my neck, I woke with a start.
Only after panting for a long while, soaked in sweat, did I realize it had been a dream.
Faint moonlight came through the window. A desolate hospital room.
I slowly rubbed my eyes.
Then I realized something was wrong.
“······Yoo Joonghyuk?”
An empty bed. Yoo Joonghyuk was nowhere in the room. The pulled-out IV line dangled alone in the air. I hurried to my feet and looked around, but couldn't sense him anywhere.
A pocket watch with a familiar design remained on the bed.
26 days remained until the ‘Great War of Saints and Demons’.
That day, Yoo Joonghyuk left <Kim Dokja’s Company>.
